items.analysis: Schwesinger led the Browns in tackles during the lopsided Week 8 loss. The 2025 second-round pick has 74 tackles (30 solo) this season, having cracked double digits in four of eight games.
items.headline: Logs 10 tackles in loss
items.notes: Schwesinger notched 10 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.

items.analysis: While Egbuka opened up the practice week with a 'DNP' on Wednesday,  Auman relays that the wideout was running full speed on the side during that session. The Buccaneers' upcoming official practice report will reveal the official Thursday participation level of Egbuka, who last saw game action in Week 6.
items.headline: Back at practice Thursday
items.notes: Egbuka, who was present for practice Thursday, was spotted testing his injured foot, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.

items.analysis: The same applies to fellow WR Mike Evans (Achilles), but on the plus side for the 49ers, Demarcus Robinson (ankle) has been designated to return from IR and could be activated ahead of Week 9 action. In any case, the official game status' of the team's top two WRs will be clarified upon the release of Friday's injury report.
items.headline: Not likely to play Sunday
items.notes: According to GM John Lynch, Samuel (hamstring) is unlikely to be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.

items.analysis: The 49ers were initially optimistic that Evans would return after the team's Week 8 bye following an absence during the Week 7 loss to Atlanta, but the veteran wide receiver apparently needs more time to recover. While official confirmation on Evans' status is unlikely to come prior to game designations being released Friday, Lynch's comments coupled with Evans' inability to practice Wednesday suggest that the wideout's fantasy managers should have an alternative option in place for Week 9.
items.headline: Likely to sit Sunday per GM
items.notes: Evans (Achilles) isn't expected to play Sunday against the Raiders, 49ers GM John Lynch said on KNBR radio Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.

items.analysis: Robinson was also deemed limited on Wednesday's estimated injury report, which gives the running back one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation before the team assigns Week 9 injury designations. If he's able to return from a two-game absence Sunday against the Bengals, he'd slot back into a complementary role behind Bijan Robinson, an assignment that Khalil Herbert handled in Weeks 7 and 8.
items.headline: Limited at practice Thursday
items.notes: Robinson (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official website reports.

items.analysis: McMillan was initially given a return timetable of 6-to-8 weeks after aggravating a PCL sprain in his left knee in Week 3. Head coach Todd Bowles said McMillan won't have his window to return from IR opened before the Buccaneers face the Bears on Sunday, and Tampa Bay will be on bye the following week, so McMillan's next chance to play won't come until Nov. 22 at Detroit.
items.headline: Won't be back until after bye
items.notes: McMillan (knee) isn't expected back until after Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.

items.analysis: "With all the evidence that we have and that they have at this point, it's not one of those things where I'm sitting back on my hands like, 'OK, am I going to play this week?'" Jacobs said. "I'm not worried about feeling like I'm going to miss any more time than I already have." Jacobs spent the first six weeks of the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Those six absences would count toward any suspension the NFL hands down to Jacobs in connection with the league's investigation into his possible violations of the league's personal conduct policy.
items.headline: Doesn't expect to miss additional action
items.notes: Jacobs doesn't anticipate missing any additional game action due to the release of additional allegations of physical and verbal abuse against him, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Head coach Mike Macdonald labeled Darnold week-to-week Wednesday while adding that Darnold isn't expected to be placed on injured reserve due to his injury. Backup Drew Lock missed the previous two games due to an elbow injury but has a chance to return Sunday against the Cardinals and take over the starting role. If Lock isn't ready to suit up, 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe could be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's NFL career.
items.headline: Considered week-to-week
items.notes: Darnold (quadriceps), who has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, is considered week-to-week, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Henley is still battling the shoulder injury that briefly sidelined him during the Week 8 loss to the Rams. Marlowe Wax and Troy Dye would likely see increased playing time if Henley ends up being unable to play in Sunday's matchup against the Texans.
items.headline: Limited in practice
items.notes: Henley (shoulder) was a limited participant in the Chargers' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Fisher hasn't played since Week 6 after undergoing thumb surgery, but he's good to go coming out of the Texans' bye week. He'll serve in a depth role at offensive tackle during Sunday's game against the Chargers.
items.headline: Turns in full practice
items.notes: Fisher (thumb) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Ruiz missed the Saints' pre-bye game against the Steelers in Paris, but the two weeks off were apparently enough to get him ready for Week 9 against Cleveland.
items.headline: Practices fully
items.notes: Ruiz (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Shepherd hasn't played since Week 4 but appears ready to return for Sunday's game against the Browns. He has 12 tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, across 175 defensive snaps this season.
items.headline: Full practice
items.notes: Shepherd (illness) practiced in full Wednesday.

items.analysis: Brown missed last Thursday night's loss to the Packers but appears ready to return for Sunday's Week 9 date with Denver. He has seven tackles (one solo) and a pass breakup across 142 defensive snaps this season.
items.headline: Full practice Wednesday
items.notes: Brown (hand) practiced fully Wednesday.

items.analysis: Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.
items.headline: Sent to IR
items.notes: The Bears placed Street (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday, Adam Jahns of AllCHGO.com reports.

items.analysis: The fourth-round rookie has been sidelined since Week 4 and has played a total of five offensive snaps this season.
items.headline: Full practice Wednesday
items.notes: Shelton (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.analysis: Banks was limited in Wednesday's session, his first of the 21-day practice window. The Saints' left tackle was injured in Week 2 against the Ravens and underwent surgery for his high ankle sprain.
items.headline: Returns to practice Wednesday
items.notes: The Saints designated Banks (ankle) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Hancock has been on IR since late September while recovering from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2 versus Detroit. The cornerback had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and if he isn't activated in that time frame, he will remain on IR for the rest of the 2026 campaign.
items.headline: Set to return to practice
items.notes: Hancock (hamstring) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Bills on Wednesday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.

items.analysis: It's not yet clear if Proctor has cleared concussion protocol, but he should be ready to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the Lions after missing Week 8 versus New England.
items.headline: Full practice Wednesday
items.notes: Proctor (concussion) practiced fully Wednesday.

items.analysis: Van Roten has been on injured reserve since Sept. 29 while recovering from a thigh injury, and the team opened his 21-day practice window. If the offensive lineman is unable to be activated in that time frame, he will be forced to remain on IR for the rest of the year.
items.headline: Nearing return to action
items.notes: Van Roten (thigh) was designated to return from injured reserve by New England on Wednesday, Matt Legros of Patriots Wire reports.

items.analysis: Herring was injured in Sunday's loss to the Patriots and didn't return to the contest. He's produced nine tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, across seven appearances this season.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Herring (neck) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Adams has been on IR since Oct. 10 while recovering from an ankle injury, but he had his 21-day practice window opened by Arizona on Wednesday. The offensive lineman will now either be activated from IR in that time frame or remain sidelined for the rest of the year.
items.headline: Designated to return from IR
items.notes: Adams (ankle) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Cardinals on Wednesday, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Thompson is still working his way back from a hamstring injury that forced the team to place him on injured reserve in late September, and he is not ready to return to practice quite yet. In his absence, P.J. Locke (concussion), Malik Hooker and Markquese Bell are poised to continue to operate as the Cowboys' primary safeties.
items.headline: Not ready to return to practice
items.notes: Thompson (hamstring) has not had his 21-day practice window opened yet, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.

items.analysis: Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign. In his absence, Theo Benedet (shoulder) will continue to operate as the team's primary option at left tackle.
items.headline: Done for season
items.notes: Jones (knee) is out for the rest of the season, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reports.

items.analysis: Payne has been sidelined since early August while recovering from a bone bruise, and he was able to return to practice Wednesday, logging a full practice. The Jets opened the safety's 21-day practice window, and it may not be long before the rookie is able to make his NFL regular-season debut.
items.headline: Back at practice
items.notes: Payne (knee) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Jets on Wednesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official website reports.

items.analysis: It was Ossai's first practice since Week 5 due to a sprained ankle. The offseason pickup has appeared in three games with the Jets this season, recording nine tackles (five solo) on 107 defensive snaps. Ossai will look to provide some more juice to the New York pass rush once cleared to return.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Ossai (ankle) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Smith was less than 100 percent to open the week after recording two total tackles (one solo) during the team's 16-0 win over the Falcons in Week 8. The safety may have picked up an ankle injury in the contest, and he will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday night's contest against Chicago.
items.headline: Limited to open week
items.notes: Smith (ankle) was a limited participant at the Buccaneers' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Sigle hasn't played since Week 4 due to a high ankle sprain. He started each of the first four games of the season and logged 26 tackles (13 solo), including 1.0 sacks, on 238 defensive snaps during that span. Sigle appears to be nearing a return to action.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Sigle (ankle) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Muhammad missed the team's Week 8 win over the Seahawks on Monday Night Football while nursing a toe injury that he suffered a week prior. The cornerback has now picked up where he left off at practice last week, logging a fourth straight limited session, and he will have two more chances to practice in full before Sunday's contest versus the Buccaneers.
items.headline: Limited participant Wednesday
items.notes: Muhammad (toe) was a limited participant at the Bears' walkthrough practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Deablo has missed back-to-back games while nursing a forearm injury that he suffered in Week 6 against Chicago. The linebacker's ability to be limited Wednesday is a step in the right direction, but he will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and move past the forearm issue before Sunday's contest versus the Bengals.
items.headline: Limited at walkthrough
items.notes: Deablo (forearm) was considered to be a limited participant at the Falcons' walkthrough practice Wednesday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official website reports.

items.analysis: McDuffie suffered a back injury during the team's 24-9 win over the Chargers in Week 8, and he has now opened the week as a nonparticipant at practice. The cornerback will have two more chances to return to practice and prove his health prior to Sunday's matchup with Washington.
items.headline: Unavailable for practice
items.notes: McDuffie (back) did not participate at the Rams' practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Newton remains on injured reserve after his 21-day practice window was opened last week. He's closing in on a return to the lineup and is needed even more now that Javon Kinlaw (knee) and Daron Payne (toe) are on injured reserve.
items.headline: Full practice Wednesday
items.notes: Newton (pectoral) practiced in full Wednesday, Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C. reports.

items.analysis: Curl notched four total tackles (one solo) during the team's 24-9 win over the Chargers in Week 8, but he may have picked up a foot injury during the contest. The safety will have two more chances to return to practice prior to Sunday's game against the Commanders.
items.headline: Misses practice Wednesday
items.notes: Curl (foot) did not participate at the Rams' practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Whittington was questionable to play in Week 8 versus the Chargers due to a back injury, but he was able to give it a go, failing to catch his only target while securing one tackle on special teams in the contest. The wide receiver will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's contest against the Commanders.
items.headline: Limited practice Wednesday
items.notes: Whittington (back) was a limited participant at the Rams' practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: The wide receiver was let go to make room for Adrian Martinez. Meiga has never appeared in a regular-season NFL game.
items.headline: Cut by Seattle
items.notes: Meiga was cut from the Seahawks' practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: Blankenship was forced to miss the team's last contest in Week 7 against the Giants while recovering from a concussion, and he may still remain in concussion protocol ahead of Week 9. The safety is also working his way back from a left-hand injury that required surgery in late October. Blankenship will have two more chances to return to practice before Sunday's contest versus the Chargers.
items.headline: Misses practice Wednesday
items.notes: Blankenship (concussion/hand) did not participate at the Texans' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Al-Shaair appears to be dealing with a groin injury coming out of Houston's bye week in Week 8. The linebacker's ability to practice in any capacity would suggest it's a minor issue, but he will have two more chances to practice in full and prove his health before Sunday's matchup with the Chargers.
items.headline: Dealing with groin injury
items.notes: Al-Shaair (groin) was a limited participant at the Texans' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: With Sam Darnold (quad) week-to-week, Martinez gives Seattle another body at quarterback. He logged one regular-season snap with San Francisco last season.
items.headline: Signs with Seattle
items.notes: The Seahawks signed Martinez to the practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: Pitre is healthy again after missing the past two games due to an AC joint injury. The 2022 second-round pick should resume his role as the team's starting slot cornerback during Sunday's game versus the Chargers.
items.headline: Full participant in practice
items.notes: Pitre (shoulder) was a full participant in Houston's practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Campbell was unable to play in the team's Week 8 loss to the Commanders while nursing hamstring and quadriceps injuries, and he appears to still be dealing with the injuries ahead of Week 9. The linebacker will have two more opportunities to return to practice prior to Sunday's matchup with the Giants.
items.headline: Unable to practice Wednesday
items.notes: Campbell (hamstring/quadriceps) did not participate at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Newsome is healthy again after missing the Week 7 win over the Texans due to a concussion. The 26-year-old signed a three-year extension with the team Tuesday and will resume his role as one of its starting cornerbacks during Sunday's matchup against the Eagles.
items.headline: Not listed on injury report
items.notes: Newsome (concussion) wasn't listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday.

items.analysis: The Falcons designated Abdullah for return to practice from their injured reserve list Tuesday, and he was able to actually get back on the practice field Wednesday, albeit in a limited capacity. He's eligible to be activated ahead of Sunday's game versus the Bengals, but he'll likely need to manage a full practice Thursday or Friday to have a realistic chance to suit up in Week 9.
items.headline: Logs limited practice Wednesday
items.notes: Abdullah (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Elliott opened the week with a limited session as a result of an apparent ankle issue. The kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT try during the team's 27-10 loss to Washington in Week 8, and he may have picked up the ankle injury during the contest. Elliott will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Giants.
items.headline: Dealing with ankle issue
items.notes: Elliott (ankle) was a limited participant at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Reid is closer to making his return after sustaining a concussion during the Week 7 loss to the Steelers. The 2018 third-round pick will still have to clear the league's concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Sunday's matchup versus the Browns. If he ends up being unable to play, Lorenzo Styles will likely start at safety in his place.
items.headline: Full go in practice
items.notes: Reid (concussion) was a full participant in New Orleans' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Shaheed missed Monday night's loss to the Bears, which allowed Tory Horton to log a season-high 43 offensive snaps, which he turned into a 3-26-0 receiving line on six targets. Horton would again be in line for WR3 duties if Shaheed needs to sit Sunday against Arizona.
items.headline: DNP on Wednesday
items.notes: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

items.analysis: Knight is in concussion protocol after playing just 18 offensive snaps in last Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) headed to injured reserve and out for at least the next four weeks, Knight figures to have a key backfield role alongside Tyler Allgeier, but it might be a challenge for Knight to gain clearance for Sunday's game against Seattle.
items.headline: Absent from practice Wednesday
items.notes: Knight (concussion) did not practice Wednesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.

items.analysis: Nixon was able to play through a shoulder injury in the team's Week 8 win over the Panthers on Thursday Night Football, but he may have tweaked the groin injury that bothered him leading up to Week 7. The cornerback's ability to practice in any capacity is a positive sign, and he'll have two more chances to practice in full before Sunday's matchup with New England.
items.headline: Limited by groin injury
items.notes: Nixon (groin) was a limited participant at the Packers' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: De Jesus joined the Chiefs as an undrafted free agent in May and was subsequently waived in August, but he is now set to rejoin the team's practice squad. The 24-year-old will now look to be elevated and make his regular-season debut.
items.headline: Returning to Kansas City
items.notes: The Chiefs signed De Jesus to their practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: Brooks was a limited participant at the team's first practice of the week as Green Bay opened his 21-day practice window Wednesday. The running back has been on IR since suffering an ankle injury in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, but he could be nearing a return to action.
items.headline: Returns to practice
items.notes: Brooks (ankle) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Packers on Wednesday, per the NFL's official transaction log.

items.analysis: Just a day after getting cut from the Browns' practice squad injured list, Means appears to be in football shape and is looking to get a chance with a new team. His last regular-season snaps came with the Saints in 2024, when he caught nine of 15 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown over seven games.
items.headline: Tries out with Chiefs
items.notes: Kansas City worked out Means (knee) on Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.

items.analysis: Corbin was released from Dallas' active roster on Tuesday but is now set to join the team's practice squad. The 26-year-old didn't see any action across the first seven weeks of the campaign and hasn't appeared in a regular-season game since 2023 with the Giants.
items.headline: Staying in Dallas
items.notes: The Cowboys signed Corbin to their practice squad Wednesday, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.

items.analysis: After Wilson continued to wear a yellow non-contact jersey at Wednesday's session, his ensuing activity level mimics what transpired last week, when he initially donned the jersey. He relayed after this past Sunday's win at Dallas that he has two broken ribs, but the addition of rest on the injury report this week indicates he's preparing to continue to play through the issue. Friday's practice report will reveal if Wilson has a designation for Sunday's game in Seattle.
items.headline: Stays limited Wednesday
items.notes: Wilson (rest/ribs) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.

items.analysis: The Seahawks ruled out Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, which places Lock in line for his second start of the campaign. However, Lock suffered a right elbow injury during Week 7 prep that left him as Seattle's emergency third quarterback the last two games. Assuming he gains clearance to suit up in Week 9, he'll be under center for Sunday's NFC West matchup.
items.headline: Listed as limited Wednesday
items.notes: Lock (right elbow) was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

items.analysis: Winters was injured in Week 6 against Green Bay and has missed the past two contests. Shemar James and DeMarvion Overshown handled linebacker duties last Sunday against the Cardinals.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Winters (calf) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.analysis: Gainwell sustained a hip injury during the Buccaneers' Week 7 win at Carolina, but he played through the issue en route to 14 carries for 88 yards. He then followed a DNP/LP/FP practice regimen last week before being listed as questionable for this past Sunday's game against the Falcons, for which he was active. Gainwell then reeled off a career-best 140 yards on 25 carries while working in tandem with fellow RB Bucky Irving. With a capped session under his belt to begin this week, Gainwell seems to be in a better spot than he was a week ago, but Friday's practice report will reveal if he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game in Chicago.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Gainwell (hip) was listed as limited on Wednesday's injury report.

items.analysis: Dallas will return to the active roster after playing in the first five contests of the year with the Vikings before being released and ultimately returning to the team as a member of the practice squad in late October. The running back has rushed four times for 14 yards and caught all four of his targets for 34 yards over seven contests with Minnesota this year, and he figures to operate in an extreme depth role behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason on Monday night versus Buffalo.
items.headline: Signed to active roster by Minnesota
items.notes: Dallas was signed to the Vikings' active roster Wednesday, Craig Peters of the team's official website reports.

items.analysis: Okereke popped up on the injury report due to a foot injury and is now in danger of missing his first game of the season. If the 2019 third-round pick ends up being unable to play in Sunday's matchup against the Broncos, Tyrel Dodson would likely get the start in his place.
items.headline: Doesn't practice Wednesday
items.notes: Okereke (foot) didn't participate in Carolina's practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: When Cole Kmet went to the Bears' injured reserve list with a season-ending knee injury following Week 7, it left the team with just two healthy tight ends on its active roster, so the move gives the club some much-needed depth at the position. As long as starter Colston Loveland and rookie third-rounder Sam Roush remain available, though, Carlson's role will likely be limited as the season progresses.
items.headline: Signing onto Bears' active roster
items.notes: Chicago signed Carlson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster Wednesday, Brendan Sugrue of USA Today reports.

items.analysis: Runyon has been on Las Vegas' injured reserve list since August with a foot injury, but it looks like he's finally on track to make his 2026 regular-season debut in Week 9. Over 13 games in 2025, the vast majority of his snaps came on special teams.
items.headline: Gets activated from IR
items.notes: The Raiders activated Runyon (foot) from their injured reserve list Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Rivers made his return to practice Wednesday, operating as a full participant at the team's first session of the week, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. The running back has been on injured reserve since late September after suffering a calf injury in Week 2 against the Giants, but he could be back in action as soon as Sunday versus the Commanders.
items.headline: Back at practice
items.notes: Rivers (calf) was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.

items.analysis: Monangai continues to be listed as a DNP due to the turf-toe injury that's held him out of the last four games. It doesn't bode well for his odds to return to action Sunday against the Buccaneers that he remains sidelined, and the Bears have a Week 10 bye, so the team may be focused on getting him healthy for the final eight contests of the campaign. D'Andre Swift will continue to lead Chicago's backfield for as long as Monangai is out, with Roschon Johnson picking up the scraps behind Swift.
items.headline: Misses Wednesday's walkthrough
items.notes: Monangai (thumb/toe) didn't participate in Wednesday's walkthrough.

items.analysis: Turpin has missed the past two contests with the injury, and his Week 9 prep isn't off on the right foot. Jonathan Mingo and Camden Brown handled reserve wideout duties behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens (hamstring) and Ryan Flournoy last Sunday against the Cardinals.
items.headline: DNP on Wednesday
items.notes: Turpin (ribs) did not practice Wednesday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.analysis: Watson was forced out of Sunday's game versus the Chargers early by a shoulder injury, and it was apparently severe enough to prematurely end his season. He had been operating as one of the Rams' top defensive backs and actually led the team in snaps at cornerback through eight weeks, so losing him is a significant blow to the club. His absence figures to create additional opportunities on the boundary for Emmanuel Forbes the rest of the way.
items.headline: Out for season
items.notes: Watson is expected to undergo shoulder surgery and to miss the remainder of the 2026 season, Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times reports.

items.analysis: The cornerback exited Sunday's win over the Chiefs with the injury and was unable to return. With Denver's cornerbacks now healthy, Abrams-Draine was relegated to a pure special-teams role in Week 8.
items.headline: DNP on Wednesday
items.notes: Abrams-Draine (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Allen played 16 snaps on special teams in Miami's 24-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 8, and he may have picked up a quadriceps injury in the process. The running back will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with Detroit.
items.headline: Limited practice Wednesday
items.notes: Allen (quadriceps) was a limited participant at the Dolphins' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Hobbs went to IR with a groin injury prior to San Francisco's regular-season debut, but it now looks like he's getting close to returning to action. The 49ers will have 21 days to officially activate him before he'd have to remain on IR for the rest of the campaign.
items.headline: Practice window opening
items.notes: The 49ers designated Hobbs (groin) for return to practice from their injured reserve list Wednesday.

items.analysis: The return man has played just two offensive snaps all season. He's recorded 274 yards on 10 kick returns and 70 yards on 12 punt returns through seven games.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Remigio (hip) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Kacmarek was limited at practice throughout the entire week before playing 19 offensive snaps and six snaps on special teams during the team's 24-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 8. The tight end may be set for a similar fate ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Lions as he continues to nurse a hamstring injury.
items.headline: Limited to open week
items.notes: Kacmarek (hamstring) was a limited participant at the Dolphins' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Holland was forced to miss the team's overtime win against the Texans in Week 7 while recovering from a concussion, but he now appears to have cleared concussion protocol. The 26-year-old will be back in his starting role in New York's secondary versus Philadelphia on Sunday.
items.headline: Not included on injury report
items.notes: Holland (concussion) was not listed on the Giants' injury report Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

items.analysis: Joseph is still waiting to make his 2026 debut as he continues to work his way back from a lingering knee injury, and his status for Week 9 is up in the air. He'll probably need to log a full practice before being activated from the reserve/PUP list, so his activity Thursday and Friday will be worth monitoring.
items.headline: Estimated as limited Wednesday
items.notes: Joseph (knee) was estimated as a limited participant on the Lions' official injury report Wednesday, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.

items.analysis: Johnson appears to be back to full health after missing the team's last two contests while nursing a neck injury. The 25-year-old will be back in his No. 2 role at tight end behind starter Isaiah Likely against the Eagles on Sunday.
items.headline: Full practice Wednesday
items.notes: Johnson (neck) was a full participant at the Giants' practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

items.analysis: Branch suffered a concussion during Sunday's game versus the Vikings, and now his status for Week 9 is in doubt. He'll need to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol before he'll be allowed to suit back up for game action, and his activity at practice Thursday and Friday could give some indication of any progress he makes ahead of Sunday's game at Miami.
items.headline: Estimated as limited participant Wednesday
items.notes: Branch (concussion) was estimated as a limited participant on the Lions' official injury report Wednesday, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.

items.analysis: Proche was cut from the Browns' practice squad in mid-October, but he has now found another opportunity in Arizona. The wide receiver played in nine regular-season contests with the Titans in 2025, reeling in six of 12 targets for 65 yards, and he'll provide the Cardinals with an additional veteran depth option with Kendrick Bourne (tibia) expected to miss the rest of the year.
items.headline: Inks deal with Arizona
items.notes: Proche was signed to the Cardinals' practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: Jefferson worked out with the team Tuesday,and he has now been added to the team's practice unit. The running back played six snaps on special teams over two regular-season contests with Arizona last year, and he will now have a chance to be elevated for a contest with the team down the road this season.
items.headline: Signed to practice squad with Arizona
items.notes: Jefferson was signed to the Cardinals' practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: Ogletree opened the week on the sideline at practice as he continues to nurse a knee issue. The tight end was able to play through the injury during the team's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars in Week 8, and he will have two more chances to return to practice before potentially giving it a go again Sunday versus the Cowboys.
items.headline: Misses practice Wednesday
items.notes: Ogletree (knee) did not participate at the Colts' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Hawkins was again unable to practice during the week, and he will be sidelined for his third consecutive game in Week 9 as he deals with a nagging knee injury. K'Von Wallace figures to continue to see increased reps in the secondary in Hawkins' stead.
items.headline: Won't play Thursday
items.notes: Hawkins (knee) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Jaguars, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.

items.analysis: Boettcher appears to be on track to return to action Sunday versus the Cowboys after missing the team's last two contests with a groin issue. The 24-year-old will likely be back in his starting role at strongside linebacker against Dallas.
items.headline: Full practice Wednesday
items.notes: Boettcher (groin) was a full participant at the Colts' practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Randall was not considered to be limited during Baltimore's walkthrough practice Wednesday but he's still on IR going into game-day. If he's not activated for Week 9, his next opportunity to make his regular-season debut would come in Week 10 versus the Chargers.
items.headline: Listed as questionable for Thursday
items.notes: Randall (neck) is officially listed as questionable for Thursday's game versus the Jaguars, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.

items.analysis: Robinson made his return to practice Wednesday, logging a limited session at the team's first gathering of the week, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. The wide receiver has been sidelined since suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2 against the Dolphins, but he could be nearing a return to action.
items.headline: Practice window opened
items.notes: Robinson (ankle) was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.

items.analysis: Wiggins did not participate during Baltimore's walkthrough practice Wednesday due to an illness, and his availability for Week 9 is now in jeopardy. If he can't suit up Thursday, it would likely mean more snaps on the boundary for veteran Chidobe Awuzie.
items.headline: Questionable for Thursday
items.notes: Wiggins (illness) is officially listed as questionable for Thursday's game versus the Jaguars, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.

items.analysis: Perryman has spent the entire regular season up to this point on IR with an undisclosed injury, but it now looks like he's nearing a return to game action. His activity at practice during the week will be worth keeping an eye on ahead of Sunday's game versus the Texans.
items.headline: Gets green light to practice again
items.notes: The Chargers designated Perryman (undisclosed) for return to practice from their injured reserve list Wednesday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Johnson was forced to miss the team's Week 8 win over the Colts while nursing an ankle injury, but he appears to be good to go for Week 9. The 25-year-old was a limited participant at the team's final practice of the week Wednesday, so he may not be back to 100 percent, but Johnson should be back in his starting role at free safety versus the Ravens.
items.headline: No injury designation for TNF
items.notes: Johnson (ankle) has no injury designation ahead of Thursday night's matchup against Baltimore.

items.analysis: Per Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site, Locke did not participate at practice Wednesday. Locke sat out five straight games prior to Week 8 because of a foot injury, and now his availability for Week 9 is up in the air after he suffered a concussion in Week 8. Whether he's able to practice Thursday or Friday should provide more insight into his status for Sunday's game against the Colts.
items.headline: Remains in concussion protocol
items.notes: Locke was still in concussion protocol Wednesday as the Cowboys began preparing for their Week 9 matchup at Indianapolis, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.

items.analysis: Walker remained limited at the team's final practice of the week Wednesday as he continues to nurse an injury to his ribs. If the defensive lineman is unable to go in Week 9, Danny Striggow and Bryan Thomas would be two top candidates to operate in more prominent roles versus Baltimore.
items.headline: Questionable for TNF
items.notes: Walker (ribs) is questionable to play Thursday night against the Ravens.

items.analysis: Per Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site, Downs did not participate at practice Wednesday. Downs hasn't missed a game yet as a pro, but his status for Sunday's game against the Colts is in doubt after he suffered a concussion in Week 8. His activity at practice Thursday and Friday should give a clearer indication as to whether he'll be able to suit up in Week 9.
items.headline: Still in concussion protocol Wednesday
items.notes: Downs remained in concussion protocol Wednesday as the Cowboys began preparing for their Week 9 matchup at Indianapolis, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.

items.analysis: Campbell had to be carted off the field on a spinal board after he took a hit to the head/neck area while making a tackle during Sunday's game versus the Vikings, and he remains in the hospital for evaluation. While updates from him and the Lions have been positive thus far, it still seems likely he'll be facing an extended absence, and barring something extraordinary, he'll at least be out in Week 9 at Miami.
items.headline: Regaining some movement
items.notes: Campbell (neck) said Wednesday that he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress with movement in his upper body, Colton Pouncy of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: After back-to-back DNPs last Wednesday and Thursday, Burks got in a limited session Friday before being cleared to play Sunday night against Philly. He ended up recording three grabs for 81 yards as the Commanders' leading receiver in the contest. Burks should play plenty of snaps the rest of the season with Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year.
items.headline: DNP on Wednesday
items.notes: Burks (foot) did not practice Wednesday, Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C. reports.

items.analysis: Bachman was released by Los Angeles on Tuesday after appearing in each of the team's last five contests, but he will now stick around as a member of the team's practice unit. Over five regular-season games this year, the wide receiver has played almost exclusively on special teams, racking up 298 kickoff-return yards and 47 yards as a punt returner.
items.headline: Signed to Rams' practice squad
items.notes: Bachman was signed to the Rams' practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: Stafford was seen leaving the locker room with his upper right arm wrapped in ice after this past Sunday's win against the Chargers. Head coach Sean McVay told Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register on Monday that Stafford has been tending to arm soreness, but the quarterback clarified the situation with Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times on Wednesday, stating that he's had his right arm wrapped in ice regularly this season. An uncapped session to begin Week 9 prep puts Stafford in the clear to continue to lead the Ram's offense Sunday in Washington.
items.headline: Practices fully Wednesday
items.notes: Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports.

items.analysis: Baker has been on the reserve/PUP list since Aug. 31 after suffering an undisclosed injury in July. The cornerback is eligible to have his 21-day practice window opened and begin practicing at any point, but he doesn't appear to be healthy enough to do so yet.
items.headline: Not ready to return to practice
items.notes: Baker (undisclosed) is not ready to return to practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.

items.analysis: Love will have to spend at least the next four games on IR, and Knight's availability for Week 9 is in doubt with him being in concussion protocol, but his coach's words signal a prominent role in Arizona's backfield may be waiting for him whenever he's ready to play again. Until then, free-agent acquisition Tyler Allgeier figures to be the primary beneficiary of Love's extended absence, but Knight should also eventually see an increased workload, especially in the passing game. Recent signee Evan Hull is also in the mix, but he has not played an offensive snap yet in 2026.
items.headline: Could see increased workload soon
items.notes: Coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that the Cardinals planned on Knight (concussion) being one of their top two backs before he and Jeremiyah Love (ankle) suffered injuries in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.

items.analysis: It's a new injury for Kirk, who made his season debut in Week 7 against the Falcons after missing the first six games with a calf injury. The Niners are coming off their bye and are hoping to get some reinforcements at wide receiver, with Demarcus Robinson (ankle) limited Wednesday, while Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) logged DNPs.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Kirk (knee) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: After being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Bryant was back on the practice field with no restrictions. With a bye looming for the Broncos in Week 10, it's unclear if the team will decide to activate the wide receiver before Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Regardless of whatever decision the team makes, Bryant appears to be fully recovered from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 4.
items.headline: Full practice Wednesday
items.notes: Bryant (ankle) was a full participant at the Broncos' practice Wednesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.

items.analysis: The Rams opened Ferguson's 21-day practice window Wednesday, as he looks to return from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Commanders. If Colby Parkinson (ribs) is unable to play for the second straight week, Ferguson would join Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen at tight end for Los Angeles.
items.headline: Officially limited Wednesday
items.notes: Ferguson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: With Lamar Jackson bound for IR with a thumb injury on his throwing hand and Tyler Huntley expected to miss the rest of the season with turf toe, coach Jesse Minter named Fagnano as the Ravens' starting quarterback for Week 9 on Tuesday. However, news broke Wednesday that Baltimore is finalizing a trade to acquire quarterback Jacoby Brissett, casting doubt on Fagnano's place in the pecking order. It looks like he'll ultimately take a back seat to Brissett starting in Week 10, but since the trade won't be finalized in time for Brissett to be available for the Ravens on Thursday, Fagnano still projects to start versus the Jaguars.
items.headline: Still in line to start Thursday
items.notes: Trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett is not expected to be available for Baltimore until Week 10, leaving Fagnano as the team's projected starting quarterback for Week 9, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.analysis: Parkinson missed the Week 8 win over the Chargers and remains sidelined for the start of Week 9 prep. Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was back at practice Wednesday and could join Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen at tight end if Parkinson is unable to face the Commanders on Sunday.
items.headline: Remains DNP on Wednesday
items.notes: Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: As expected, Ferguson was unavailable for practice as he worked off to the side with the team's training staff. The tight end is working through a low-ankle sprain that he suffered during the team's 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in Week 8, and his availability for Sunday's matchup against the Colts is in question. Ferguson will have two more chances to return to practice this week, but if he can't go for Week 9, Brevyn Spann-Ford would be a top candidate to take over as the primary tight end for Dallas.
items.headline: Officially unavailable for practice
items.notes: Ferguson (ankle) did not participate at the Cowboys' practice Wednesday, Patrik Walker of the team's official site reports.

items.analysis: The running back went down with the injury in the Saints' pre-Week 8 bye loss to the Steelers in Paris back in Week 7. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) still on injured reserve and looking unlikely to play Sunday against the Browns, New Orleans added Audric Estime to a backfield that also includes Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Donaldson (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: It was Bosa's first practice since suffering a knee injury in Week 2 that has forced him to miss the last five contests. Coming out of the Week 8 bye, the Niners are getting healthy. In two games this season, Bosa has seven tackles (three solo) across 76 defensive snaps.
items.headline: Limited in practice Wednesday
items.notes: Bosa (knee) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.
items.headline: Set for increased reps at practice
items.notes: Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.

items.analysis: Wicks hasn't practiced due to an ankle injury since preparation for a Week 6 matchup with the Panthers, missing the last two games in the process. He likely will need to mix into drills in some capacity Thursday and/or Friday to put himself in a position to return to action Sunday versus the Giants.
items.headline: DNP on Wednesday
items.notes: Wicks (ankle) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Smith's lack of activity to kick off Week 9 prep doesn't come as a surprise, as he wasn't present during the media-access portion of Wednesday's session. He hasn't practiced since his last appearance in a Week 6 loss to the Panthers, when he went for seven catches (on 14 targets) for 75 yards and one touchdown. If he's able to put himself in a position to play Sunday against the Giants, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from QB Joe Milton, who is replacing Tanner McKee as the starter.
items.headline: No practice Wednesday
items.notes: Smith (hamstring) didn't practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Barkley's DNP to begin Week 9 prep was forecast by his lack of presence during the open portion of Wednesday's session. He continues to deal with the hamstring and back injuries that bothered him last week, but he still was able to play this past Sunday at Washington, log a 32 percent snap share and turn 14 touches into 54 yards from scrimmage and one TD. If he follows a similar practice regimen as last week, Barkley also will sit out Thursday before returning as a limited participant Friday.
items.headline: Doesn't practice Wednesday
items.notes: Barkley (hamstring/back) officially didn't practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: White became a roster casualty after the Raiders needed to clear a spot for tight end Carter Runyon (foot), who was reinstated from injured reserve after his 21-day practice window came to a close. Though he made a splash earlier in the season with seven receptions for 108 yards and three touchdowns on 14 targets through the Raiders' first five games, White had seen his playing time and production drop off dramatically over the subsequent three contests, during which he was limited to just a four-yard reception on five targets. With Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton recently making their returns from injured reserve, White's role wasn't likely to grow had he stuck around in Las Vegas.
items.headline: Cut by Las Vegas
items.notes: The Raiders released White on Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic earlier Wednesday that Parsons will participate in individual drills in his return to practice. Before that could go down, though, the Packers designated him for return from the reserve/PUP list, per the NFL's transaction log. According to Ryan Wood of USA Today, Parson declined to "pinpoint a day" for his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025 at Denver, but Green Bay now has a 21-day window in which to evaluate him and determine when that'll occur.
items.headline: Limited in return to practice
items.notes: Parsons (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Wednesday.

items.analysis: After the Patriots opened up his 21-day evaluation window, Hollins took the field for his first practice since Week 4. Hollins will be eligible for activation from IR at any point, but unless he upgrades to full participation by the end of the week, he could have a tough time gaining clearance for Sunday's matchup with the Packers. Through New England's first four games before he sustained a calf injury, Hollins produced a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets.
items.headline: Limited in return to practice
items.notes: Hollins (calf) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice after being designated for return from injured reserve.

items.analysis: Garrett has been on injured reserve since aggravating a left knee injury that required arthroscopic surgery in Week 1. In order to be able to practice Wednesday, the Rams designated him for return from IR, per the NFL's transaction log. Garrett's activity level bears watching as the week goes on to get a sense of his odds to play Sunday at Washington.
items.headline: Will practice Wednesday
items.notes: Head coach Sean McVay said Garrett (knee) will practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Since sitting out Weeks 3 and 4 due to a thumb injury, Taylor has played north of 50 percent of the snaps on offense in each of the Jets' last four games, cobbling together a 15-138-2 receiving line on 20 targets over that stretch. Provided the back issue doesn't prevent him from practicing Thursday and Friday, Taylor should be able to handle his usual role this Sunday in Kansas City.
items.headline: Limited to begin Week 9 prep
items.notes: Taylor was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a back injury.

items.analysis: Early in this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson exited the game to get checked for a concussion following a helmet-to-helmet hit, but he was cleared to re-enter the contest after missing just four offensive snaps. However, after he had some late-surfacing symptoms, Watson entered concussion protocol Tuesday and was a spectator for the Browns' first Week 9 session. According to Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, Watson "felt a lot better" Wednesday and was involved in meetings, but Shedeur Sanders took all the reps with the first-team offense. Sanders appears to be trending toward starting Sunday against the Saints, as Monken acknowledged that it will be difficult for Watson to play even if he ends up clearing the protocol late in the week, per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram.
items.headline: Unable to practice Wednesday
items.notes: The Browns listed Watson (concussion) as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Wilson also donned such a jersey last week, when he was listed as limited on all three of the Cardinals' injury reports due to a rib injury. He then missed a spell from the second and into the third quarters this past Sunday in Dallas, after which it was revealed he's tending to two broken ribs. Wilson still put up an 8-111-1 line on 15 targets in that contest, and assuming he's able to suit up Sunday at Seattle, he'll be one of new starting QB Gardner Minshew's top available pass catchers along with TE Trey McBride.
items.headline: Wearing non-contact jersey at practice
items.notes: Wilson (ribs) wore a yellow non-contact jersey at Wednesday's practice, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.

items.analysis: Boston made appearances on the injury report in Weeks 6 and 7 due to a foot issue, but he's tending to a new health concern coming out of this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. The rookie wideout will have two more chances this week to upgrade to full practice, and if he does, he should head into Sunday's game in New Orleans without an injury designation.
items.headline: Limited by calf injury Wednesday
items.notes: Boston was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

items.analysis: The Saints cited rest and a back injury -- the latter of which impacted his practice reps in each of the three games before the team's Week 8 bye -- as the reasons for Kamara's absence to begin Week 9 prep. During that three-contest stretch, he tallied 27 touches for 137 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD. Kamara will have two more opportunities to practice this week and put himself in a position to avoid a designation for Sunday's contest against the Browns.
items.headline: DNP due to rest, back
items.notes: Kamara (rest/back) didn't practice Wednesday.

items.analysis: Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak said that he "absolutely" believes that Jeanty can be a bell cow running back, but at least for the time being, he looks like he'll be part of a timeshare with Washington. Jeanty has seen his carry count drop or hold steady in each successive game since Week 1, culminating in the 2025 first-round pick logging just two carries in this past Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets, while Washington carried a career-high 25 times for 83 yards. The split in carries may not be quite as dramatic in weeks to come, but Washington appears to have earned himself a sizable piece of the pie while he's averaging 4.3 yards per tote to Jeanty's 3.1 mark through eight games. Jeanty remains the Raiders' clear cut top option on passing downs over Washington, who has recorded just three receptions for 11 yards on six targets so far this season.
items.headline: Workload breakdown a 'week-to-week' decision
items.notes: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that the breakdown in carries between Washington and Ashton Jeanty will be determined on a week-to-week basis, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: After making a visit to the hospital during last Thursday's win against the Panthers, Watson was able to return and finished with eight catches (on 10 targets) for 113 yards. Afterward, he was revealed to have a broken rib, which likely will be an injury he plays through while managing pain tolerance. In any case, Friday's injury report will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at New England.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Watson (ribs) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Ferguson has been out since sustaining an ankle injury against the Broncos in Week 3. He has upward of 21 days to be activated off IR. A return in Week 9 may be optimistic at this stage and will hinge on his practice participation for the remainder of the week. Regardless, Ferguson is trending toward being back on the field in the near future.
items.headline: Practice window opens Wednesday
items.notes: Ferguson (ankle) is returning to practice Wednesday, opening his 21-day window to return, Gary Klein of the LA Times reports.

items.analysis: Pickens was limited by shoulder and hamstring injuries last week, but he was able to suit up this past Sunday against the Cardinals, logging a 57 percent snap share and gathering in two of four targets for 48 yards. As Week 9 prep kicks off, he's being listed with only the hamstring issue, which continues to impact his on-field work. Pickens will have two more chances to get back to full Thursday and Friday before Dallas potentially tags him with a designation for Sunday's contest at Indianapolis.
items.headline: Limited in Wednesday's practice
items.notes: Pickens (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.analysis: Help is on the way for the Broncos' passing game, as Bryant is making progress toward a return now that his 21-day practice window has been opened. Though the wideout will be back on the field to begin Week 9 prep, it's unclear if the Broncos intend to activate him from IR ahead of Sunday's game at Carolina.
items.headline: Cleared to resume practicing
items.notes: The Broncos designated Bryant (ankle) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.

items.analysis: McCaffrey toughed out what eventually was revealed to be a mild left hamstring strain during a Week 7 loss in Atlanta, when he finished with 13 touches for 100 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD. With the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he said Wednesday that he feels "great," but chances for on-field work await for him Thursday and Friday.
items.headline: May practice, play this week
items.notes: McCaffrey (hamstring) said Wednesday that he has a chance to practice this week and play Sunday against the Raiders, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Smythe will take over for the recently released Daniel Carlson. A native of Northern Ireland, Smythe went 12-for-16 on field goals over six games for the Saints in 2025.
items.headline: Officially taking over as kicker
items.notes: Coach Kellen Moore announced Wednesday that Smyth will be the Saints' kicker in Week 9, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Rice got back in the fold in Week 8 to the tune of an 7-53-1 line after missing time with a hamstring injury, and he is limited to start preparation for the Jets. The Chiefs could be exercising caution with their top receiver, who also rehabbed from knee surgery during the offseason. A limited session Wednesday does not mean his Week 9 status is in jeopardy, but his participation over the coming days will be telling.
items.headline: Limited Wednesday
items.notes: Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Kelce logged a limited session this past Thursday before practicing fully a day later. He then approached Week 8 action without an injury designation, en route to recording a 78 percent offensive snap share and catching five of his seven targets for 67 yards in the Chiefs' 28-24 loss to the Broncos. Chances are, the tight end's listed limitations Wednesday were maintenance-related, and he will now have two more chances to work fully ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.headline: Limited practice Wednesday
items.notes: Kelce (ankle) was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: The rookie first-round pick hadn't practiced since Aug. 13 due to a right hamstring strain, but he's closing in on making his NFL debut now that he's officially had his 21-day window opened. Given that he's beginning Week 9 prep with a limited practice following a lengthy layoff, Tyson may not be in play to be activated for this Sunday's game against the Browns. The Saints will see how Tyson looks in practice the next two days before deciding on his availability for the Week 9 game.
items.headline: Limited in return Wednesday
items.notes: Tyson (hamstring) had his 21-day practice window opened and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session.

items.analysis: Etienne has missed the required four games on IR due to a strained left hamstring, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he hasn't gained clearance to mix into drills. Moore told Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana on Monday that Etienne has a chance to return to practice this week, but with no on-field work to begin Week 9 prep, he seems to be on the outside looking in to have enough time to be activated for Sunday's contest against the Browns.
items.headline: Not practicing yet
items.notes: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints haven't opened Etienne's (hamstring) practice window just yet, Jeff Nowak of WWL Louisiana reports.

items.analysis: Jeanty is averaging just 3.1 yards per tote on the season and has seen his carry count gradually decline with each successive game. After rushing a season-high 23 times in a Week 1 win over the Dolphins, Jeanty logged just two carries (for nine yards) in this past Sunday's win over the Jets, while Washington handled 25 carries (for 83 yards). According to McFadden, Kubiak said that he believes Jeanty can "absolutely" be a bell cow running back, but the second-year player out of Boise State looks like he'll be part of a timeshare with Washington until his production on the ground improves. Jeanty is still locked in as the Raiders' clear top back on passing downs, as he ranks first or tied for first with all NFL running backs in targets (49), receptions (37), receiving yards (376) and receiving touchdowns (three).
items.headline: Workload to be decided on week-to-week basis
items.notes: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that the breakdown in carries between Jeanty and Mike Washington will be determined on a week-to-week basis, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: The Giants are coming off of their bye and preparing for the Eagles, and Skattebo was not available to practice as the week got underway. Skattebo tweaked his hamstring on his last carry of the game against the Texans in Week 7. His status in practice the remainder of the week will be crucial given the Giants' shorthandedness in the backfield. Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers are the healthy options at RB beyond Skattebo.
items.headline: Does not practice Wednesday
items.notes: Skattebo (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.

items.analysis: In addition to a foot injury, Wright was listed with the same quad issue on the Dolphins' Week 8 injury report but proceeded to log three full practices before playing in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Though he played just 13 total snaps between offense and special teams in Week 8, Wright apparently emerged from the contest with his quad injury still bothering him. He'll have two more chances to get back to full practice participation prior to this Sunday's game against the Lions.
items.headline: Sits out first Week 9 practice
items.notes: Wright (quadriceps) was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.

items.analysis: St. Brown made a brief exit during this past Sunday's win against the Vikings due to an undisclosed injury but was able to return, finishing with seven catches (on eight targets) for 46 yards and one carry for 10 yards. The nature of the health concern has been revealed, but his ability to practice in some capacity Wednesday generally bodes well for his status ahead of Sunday's game at Miami.
items.headline: Limited at Wednesday's walkthrough
items.notes: St. Brown was a limited participant at Wednesday's walkthrough due to a rib injury, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.

items.analysis: Franklin started the week as a nonparticipant in practice Wednesday and hasn't played since Week 6 after suffering a hairline fracture in his shin. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur added Wednesday that the 30-year-old is making progress in his recovery and he hopes Franklin can return soon. The ninth-year pro has 41 tackles (18 solo), one pass deflection and one forced fumble in six games this season.
items.headline: Does not practice Wednesday
items.notes: Franklin (shin) did not participate in practice Wednesday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Samuel injured his right hamstring during a Week 5 win at Seattle, resulting in two missed games before the 49ers' Week 8 bye. Head coach Kyle Shanahan relayed to Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area on Oct. 26 that Samuel has a chance to return this Sunday against the Raiders, but Shanahan's tone was a bit different Wednesday, when he told Vic Tafur and Matt Barrows of The Athletic that Samuel doesn't seem as close to playing as fellow WR Mike Evans (Achilles).
items.headline: No practice Wednesday
items.notes: Samuel (hamstring) won't take part in practice Wednesday, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.

items.analysis: Evans sat out a Week 7 loss in Atlanta after aggravating a right Achilles injury in Week 6 against the Commanders, and while there's an expectation that he'll be back after a Week 8 bye, he'll kick off this week with a DNP. He thus will have two more chances to mix into drills ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Raiders.
items.headline: Won't practice Wednesday
items.notes: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans (Achilles/ribs) won't practice Wednesday, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports.

items.analysis: Montgomery missed Houston's last two games before a Week 8 bye, and he doesn't look like he'll be ready to return to action any sooner than Nov. 15, when the Texans face the Browns on the road. With Montgomery set to miss another game, Woody Marks is poised to maintain a lead role out of the backfield. While Montgomery was sidelined the previous two contests, Marks averaged 81.0 scrimmage yards on 18.5 touches per game.
items.headline: Out for third straight game
items.notes: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that Montgomery (groin) has made some progress but is still viewed as week-to-week and will remain out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.

items.analysis: Three key vets are not taking part in the first practice out of the bye Wednesday as McCaffrey, Mike Evans (Achilles/ribs) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) are all sidelined for this session. McCaffrey has been dealing with a hamstring issue since the Week 7 game in Atlanta. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that McCaffrey is "not going today but hopefully a chance [Thursday]." The next few days of practice will be telling for McCaffrey's status going into Sunday's game against the Raiders.
items.headline: Will not practice Wednesday
items.notes: McCaffrey (hamstring) will not participate in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of Bay Area News Group reports.

items.analysis: Williams missed Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury, which likely occurred at some point during the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers. However, head coach Todd Monken said he is "optimistic" that the 30-year-old will be ready for Week 9. Williams will need to upgrade his practice status by Friday for a chance to play.
items.headline: Not practicing Wednesday
items.notes: Williams (hamstring) did not participate in practice Wednesday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

items.analysis: Wicks has missed the last two games with an ankle injury and is trending towards being a DNP to start Week 9. If he's unable to ramp up his activity in the coming days, another missed game would be very much on the table. The Eagles are readying Joe Milton at quarterback, and he could be without both Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring), who was also absent from Wednesday's viewing period.
items.headline: Not seen at practice
items.notes: Wicks (ankle) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Bailey was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, which is a step up from last week's three DNPs. The 23-year-old missed Week 8 with a groin injury suffered in Week 7 against Miami. Should the rookie continue to progress well throughout the week, he could have a shot at returning for Week 9.
items.headline: Limited in practice Wednesday
items.notes: Bailey (groin) was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Smith has missed four of the last five contests due to a lingering hamstring injury, and until he's able to mix into drills again, he may not be a candidate to be active on game days. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye after Sunday's matchup with the Giants, so the team could be focusing on getting him healthy for Week 11 and beyond. In any case, fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also wasn't seen Wednesday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore as the healthy options at the position on the active roster.
items.headline: Not present Wednesday
items.notes: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: Meanwhile, Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) has been deemed questionable for the contest after being listed as a DNP on each of the Jaguars' injury reports, Monday through Wednesday. Given that Tuten has been the team's lead back this season, his playing status (and potential workload, if he's active Thursday) will provide valuable context related to the Week 9 fantasy prospects of Rodriguez, who could assume a larger backfield role versus Baltimore if Tuten ends up out or limited.
items.headline: No Week 9 injury designation
items.notes: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Ravens.

items.analysis: Though Meyers was limited in practice, the Jaguars are not listing him on the injury report going into Thursday's game. The veteran has battled through bumps and bruises throughout the season but has yet to miss a game. He'll be good to go for Week 9 in Charm City.
items.headline: Good to go for TNF
items.notes: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) does not carry an injury designation going into Thursday's game at the Ravens.

items.analysis: The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein Njoku can be evaluated for a return to the 53-man roster. The veteran tight end has been out of action since sustaining the fibula injury Week 2, but if he's able to turn in a full practice at some point over the next three days, he could have a chance at being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans. Once he's back in the fold, Njoku could push Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden for snaps at tight end.
items.headline: Cleared to resume practicing
items.notes: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Njoku (fibula) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.

items.analysis: Barkley may still be tending to the hamstring and back issues that he impacted his practice reps last week, but Wednesday's injury report will reveal if he indeed was a non-participant and also the reason for his absence. Jaydon Blue is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell tallied 11 carries for 34 yards and four catches (on six targets) for three yards while splitting the backfield with Barkley this past Sunday at Washington.
items.headline: Not spotted at practice
items.notes: Barkley wasn't present for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.

items.analysis: The undrafted rookie receiver out of TCU had previously spent time with Denver in the offseason, appearing in all three preseason games while catching three of four targets for 40 yards. After failing to make the Broncos' roster heading into Week 1, Manjack had been a free agent before landing an opportunity with the Jets.
items.headline: Joins Jets practice squad
items.notes: The Jets signed Manjack to the practice squad Wednesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.

items.analysis: Mitchell-Paden failed to appear in a 2026 regular-season game after signing to the Texans' practice squad to begin the campaign. In two games with the Saints in 2025, the 27-year-old recorded one reception for 14 yards on 55 total snaps (33 offensive).
items.headline: Released from PS
items.notes: The Texans released Mitchell-Paden from the practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: For the third day in a row, Tuten went down as a non-participant on the Jaguars' injury report, even though head coach Liam Coen suggested the running back would practice in a limited fashion Wednesday, per Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network. The coach added that the Jaguars will be viewing Tuten as a game-time decision for Thursday's tilt, with his availability perhaps hinging on how he fares during a gameday workout. If Tuten ends up missing his first game of the season or is active but available in only a limited capacity, Chris Rodriguez would be in store for a larger role out of the backfield.
items.headline: Questionable for Thursday after no practice
items.notes: Tuten (ankle/foot) is listed questionable for Thursday's game against the Ravens.

items.analysis: Sobkowicz was on Houston's practice squad for the first five weeks of the season before being cut in October. The 24-year-old has yet to make a regular-season appearance for the Texans. Landing back on the team's practice squad, the undrafted rookie has a long way to go before making his NFL debut.
items.headline: Signs to practice squad
items.notes: The Texans signed Sobkowicz to the practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: Brissett was set to become a free agent this offseason and was demoted from the starting role earlier this week, making him an expendable piece for the Cardinals, who will move forward with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck as their quarterbacks. Baltimore, meanwhile, had a critical need for an experienced signal-caller after losing  Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (foot) to injuries that will send both quarterbacks to injured reserve and potentially keep them out for the rest of the season, so Brissett will fill a void. Since the trade won't be made official for a few more days, Brissett won't be available for the Ravens' Thursday night game against the Jaguars. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will direct the Baltimore offense against Jacksonville, but Brissett could step in as the Ravens' new starter beginning with a Week 10 matchup against the Chargers.
items.headline: Shipped to Baltimore
items.notes: The Ravens are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals that will send Brissett to Baltimore, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The deal is expected to be completed over the weekend.

items.analysis: Bowman hasn't played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 6 against Chicago. Now with a full practice, the 23-year-old is on track to play Sunday against the Bengals. The second-year pro has six tackles (five solo) and two pass deflections in four games this season.
items.headline: Estimated as full participant
items.notes: Bowman was estimated as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.analysis: Henry was unable to return to Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins after exiting in the second quarter due to the foot issue. The Patriots haven't provided many details regarding the severity of the injury, but Henry will be sidelined as the team begins Week 9 prep. Henry will have two more chances to potentially practice this week before the Patriots decide whether he'll take a designation into Sunday's game against the Packers.
items.headline: Sitting out first practice of Week 9
items.notes: Henry (foot) wasn't on the field for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.

items.analysis: Haskins spent the majority of the 2026 season on New England's practice squad before being cut on Oct. 17. Last season with the Chargers, the 26-year-old recorded 17 rushing attempts for 47 yards, averaging 2.8 yards per carry. He also had four receptions for 13 yards.
items.headline: Signs to practice squad
items.notes: The Browns signed Haskins to their practice squad Wednesday.

items.analysis: Ryan has suited up seven times for the Browns so far this season. With another elevation ahead of Week 9, the 23-year-old is eligible to play for Cleveland once again against the Saints. He has spent the majority of his in-game snaps on special teams.
items.headline: Signs to active roster
items.notes: The Browns signed Ryan to the active roster Wednesday from the team's practice squad.

items.analysis: Just two days after announcing that McKee would draw a fourth straight start this weekend, head coach Nick Sirianni appears to have changed his tune. The Eagles' decision to move forward with Milton comes after McKee went 0-3 as a starter while completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 5.6 yards per attempt and a 2:2 TD:INT since replacing Jalen Hurts (calf) atop the depth chart. Since McKee is set to become a free agent next spring and may not be part of the Eagles' long-term plans, he could end up serving as the No. 3 quarterback if the team wants to give rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton the opportunity to suit up on game days.
items.headline: Benched for Joe Milton in Week 9
